chunks: Hakim ibn Dawud narrated to me from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Any believer whose eyes shed tears for the killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), with a tear running down his cheek, Allah will prepare for him thereby rooms in Paradise, dwelling in them for long ages.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for crying over the death of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith underscores the profound spiritual merit of *buka'* (weeping) over Imam al-Husayn’s martyrdom, a practice central to Shia devotional identity since the early centuries. The promise of 'high chambers' (*ghuraf*) signifies a superior rank in Paradise, linking the emotional act of mourning directly to eternal reward and intercessory status within Shia eschatology.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 9. Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali, from ‘Alā ibn Razīn Al-Qallā, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said:

Any believer who cries over Ḥusain (a.s.) with (even) one tear running down his cheek will be rewarded by Allāh for that tear; he will be made to dwell in rooms in Paradise where he will stay for long ages.
